newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Bomb blast at Albanian cafe injures 20.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast at Albanian cafe injures 20.

text.p: At least 20 people were injured when a bomb exploded at a cafe on the main square of the Albanian capital Tirana on Monday, witnesses said.

The cafe on Skanderbeg Square was a known rendezvous point for Socialists, the main opposition to President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party in June 29 elections, called to end turbulence in the impoverished Balkan country.
Berisha, fighting for his political life in the coming vote, denounced the blast.
"The president assured those injured that those responsible for this act will soon be punished," Berisha's office said a statement read on state television.
Witnesses said they saw two young men enter the cafe with a parcel just after midday.
One went to the toilet and the explosion came a minute later, causing the balcony of the second storey to collapse, scattering customers and knocking over tables, chairs and umbrellas.
Police said it had apparently been caused by an explosive called tritol, widely used in formerly communist Albania.
The Cafe Freskia, owned by the Socialist Party leader and state secretary for the Interior Ministry Lush Perpali, was known to be frequented by Socialist supporters.
A story in the pro-Berisha newspaper Albania on Sunday carried the headline "Lush Perpali's restaurant will be blown up".
Police sealed off the area surrounding the cafe, which adjoins the ministries of defence and mineral resources and opens onto the back court of the Socialist Party headquarters.
An injured customer called Agron said there were some 30 to 50 clients in the cafe at the time of the blast, shortly after midday, and about 20 had been injured.
"This is Berisha's typical fundamentalist action because it is well known this cafe is frequented by Socialist supporters," Agron said. "This is a terrorist act."
But Western diplomats were cautious in assigning motives for the blast, the biggest in Tirana since one before May, 1996 elections which killed four people.
"Some will say this was politically motivated and others will say it was criminally motivated," one said. "The lines are blurring."

Agron Shahu, an officer at Tirana's military hospital, said three of the injured had been treated there and released. A nurse at Tirana's Emergency Hospital said 17 victims had been released after treatment while one, Arjan Shameti, who rented the cafe, was being treated for serious injuries.
Dr Krenar Lila, a doctor in the intensive care ward, told Albania's ATA agency that the most of the injured had superficial wounds. But added that four "were in a critical situation".

Albania has been awash with weapons and military ordnance since armouries were looted in March during riots that swept much of the country, ignited when thousands of people lost their life savings in the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes.

People blamed Berisha and his Democratic Party-led government for the collapse, forcing Berisha to agree to the formation of a multi-party government of national reconciliation and to hold early elections set for June 29.
